Whirlpool Corporation, Ottawa Division RMP Executive Summary 

Stationary source and regulated substance handled

Whirlpool Corporation owns and operates a household appliance manufacturing facility in Ottawa, Ohio. The facility uses R600A, isobutane (2-Methylpropane), CAS # 75-28-5, to charge appliances with refrigerant. The isobutane is received by truck and stored in a 6,565-gallon above-ground pressure vessel that is filled to no more than 85% capacity, then transferred to the refrigerant charging areas via piping. Isobutane is a regulated flammable substance under the EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) Chemical Accident Prevention rule (40 CFR 68), and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Process Safety Management (PSM) standard (29 CFR 1910.119). The facility has more than a threshold quantity of isobutane in a process; therefore, the refrigerant charging process is subject to EPA RMP, OSHA PSM, and the Accidental Release Prevention Program under the Ohio Administrative Code (OAC 3745-104). The facility is subject to Program 3 requirements under EPA RMP and the Ohio Accidental Release Prevention Program. The maximum amount of isobutane stored at this facility is 26,000 pounds. 

Whirlpool is resubmitting its RMP due to a change that required a revised Process Hazard Analysis (PHA). In October 2024, new piping was installed for an isobutane charging station in the manufacturing area of the facility. The change did not require an increase to isobutane inventories at the facility; however, it did impact the facilitys process hazard analysis (PHA). A PHA for this project was conducted on September 4, 2024, using the Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) methodology, as well as a checklist for the evaluation of human factors and facility siting. The pre-startup safety review (PSSR) for the new piping was completed on October 8, 2024. This RMP revision is being submitted within six months of this change since it necessitated a revised PHA as required by

40 CFR 68.190(b)(5) and OAC 3745-104-49(B)(5). 

Our facility has taken all necessary steps to comply with the accidental release prevention requirements set out under 40 CFR part 68 of the EPA RMP rule and the Ohio Accidental Release Prevention Program. The following sections briefly describe the elements of the accidental release prevention program implemented at the Whirlpool Corporation Ottawa Division facility.

Accidental release prevention and Emergency response policies

Accidental release prevention:
The isobutane storage vessel/bulkhead is protected to the East and South by a large retention pond with a driveway/parking area to the North and West.

An 8-foot-high chain link fence has been installed around the main property with a coded gate and around the isobutane storage vessel to prevent unauthorized access.

Only trained and authorized personnel are permitted to enter the isobutane storage vessel area and operate the equipment. All operators are trained in the operating procedures for isobutane offloading activities and manufacturing (e.g., equipment charging) operations that are part of the isobutane covered process, including safe work practices such as lockout tagout, line breaking, and hot work.

Jersey barriers have been installed around the isobutane storage vessel/bulkhead every 6 feet to eliminate the potential for an accidental or intentional vehicle strike.

An emergency shutoff is located on the tank, bulkhead, and various locations throughout the systems including at the end use, charging stations.

A handheld lower explosive limit (LEL)/Oxygen (O2) meter is used during isobutane offloading and repair operations. The meters are bump tested prior to each use by the technicians. The technicians are trained in the use of these meters, including the proper placement for monitoring.

In the event of a fire, the vessel has a certified 3 stage relief/blow off valves in place to prevent a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE).

Drager P

assive Infrared sensors (PIR) 7000 OV/LEL meters are placed in various positions within the vessel, bulkhead and charging cells. The meters are set to alarm at 10% and 25% of the LEL. A shutdown permissive is associated with the 25% LEL alarm where the isobutane flow automatically stops upon detection of 25% LEL. It also sends a signal to the security desk, at which point security staff will immediately notify the shift Emergency Coordinator.

The isobutane storage area is electrically classified, and all tools used in or near the covered process are non-sparking. Radios and cell phones are certified for Zone 2, Group IIA use.

There are flags located on the south side of the facility and a windsock mounted on the roof to guide evacuees and/or first responders.

Emergency Response Policies:
It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances. In the unlikely event that such a release was to occur, we are coordinated with the local fire department, Ottawa Police Department, and Putnam County Sheriffs Office, who will provide trained emergency response personnel to control and mitigate the effects of a release. 

General accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps

Our facility has taken all the necessary steps to comply with the accidental release prevention requirements set out under the EPA RMP Rule, OSHA PSM Standard, and the Ohio Accidental Release Prevention Plan. 

As part of the accidental release prevention program, hazards of the process are identified through process hazard analyses (PHA) using the hazard and operability studies (HAZOP) methodology based on detailed process safety information. 

The process includes safety features such as fixed LEL detectors; handheld LEL/O2 detectors; flow meters, alarms, and trips; automatic shutdown devices; pressure gauges with automatic shutdowns for high and low pressure; continuous exhaust system with alarm; physical barriers aroun

d the isobutane vessel, and safety relief valves. 

Additionally, Whirlpool has administrative measures in place at the facility for accident prevention, including: written procedures on equipment maintenance and management of change; an inspection matrix which includes daily, weekly, monthly inspections, tests, and maintenance activities for process equipment; written operating procedures; the Plant Emergency Plan; and role-specific and hazard communication training program for operations, maintenance, air monitoring, and emergency coordinator personnel.

Five-year accident history 
There have been no significant accidental releases meeting the RMP accident reporting criteria at this facility in the past five years.

The emergency response program
Whirlpool maintains a written Plant Emergency Plan that details processes for identifying an accidental release and activating notification mechanisms to alert local response agencies (e.g., fire department and police department) of the need for response. The facility is a non-responding source, meaning it relies on local emergency responders in the event of an accidental release.

The initial step regardless of the release volume is to evacuate personnel out of the building to assembly points to the west and north of the building.

In the event of a small/incidental release, there are multiple ball valves inline that can be shut down to stop the flow of isobutane from the vessel to the building. At which time, automatic evacuation fans would activate within the building and vacuum out any fugitive vapors. For a large, catastrophic release, all personnel would be evacuated to the assembly points and the Ottawa Fire Department notified via 911. Their Incident Commander (IC) would take over control of the release and notification of off-site resources.

Planned changes to improve safety
Recent changes to improve safety include: the installation of a physical barrier to prevent powered industrial vehicle collision in the Obe
ron Charge/Repair Cell area, the installation of a guard to protect charge boards, and the addition of a tie-in from the nitrogen gas flow meter to the natural gas valve opening as part of PROVAC.
